octen.title: SK Hynix plans US$45 billion of dividends, buyback after posting 7-fold jump in Q3 profit - The Business Times
octen.snippet:
SK Hynix plans US\$45 billion of dividends, buyback after posting 7-fold jump in Q3 profit

SK Hynix has prioritised long-term contracts with customers including Nvidia

Published Wed, Oct 28, 2026 · 08:03 AM— Updated Wed, Oct 28, 2026 · 11:18 AM

 

SK Hynix reported an operating profit of 83.3 trillion won for the September quarter, beating projections by more than 7%. PHOTO: REUTERS

SK HYNIX unveiled plans to return about US\$45 billion more to shareholders after profit surged a stronger-than-expected seven-fold, reflecting the resilience of an AI infrastructure rollout that is propelling memory chip demand.

The world’s second-biggest memory chipmaker reaffirmed it expects shortages of the components crucial to Nvidia accelerators to persist through at least 2030, propping up prices. On Wednesday (Oct 28), it reported an operating profit of 83.3 trillion won (US\$62.5 billion) for the September quarter, beating projections by more than 7 per cent.

The company also laid out plans to return 60 trillion won to shareholders in the remainder of the fiscal year through buybacks and dividends, on top of a previously announced 40 trillion won. Much of that stems from gains it locked in after a sale of stock in Kioxia Holdings earlier in 2026.

SK Hynix’s shares rose more than 7 per cent in early Seoul trading, while rival Samsung Electronics gained more than 8 per cent.

The results bolstered hopes for sustained profits from a surge in demand for memory from AI developers building data centres.
